label: A May weekend day: the duck curve, negative prices and a battery
context: Animate one average May 2025 weekend day in Germany (real averages from Energy-Charts), hour 0 to 24 on the x-axis, as a cursor sweeps the day (about 14 s for the day, then 6 s for the battery phase, loop). Top panel, GW (0 to 60): draw progressively up to the cursor: load (ink #04204B line): 0h 40.5, 2h 37.5, 4h 37.2, 6h 38.6, 8h 44.2, 10h 47.5, 12h 47.7, 14h 44.5, 16h 43.8, 18h 46.3, 20h 46.2, 22h 43.9, 24h 40.5. Wind (blue #2F6FD0 area from 0): 0h 14.0, 4h 13.5, 8h 10.0, 12h 10.3, 16h 11.2, 20h 13.2, 24h 14. Solar (amber #E3A21A area stacked on wind): 0 until 6h, 6h 2.4, 8h 16.6, 10h 28.8, 12h 32.0, 14h 30.0, 16h 23.5, 18h 10.6, 20h 0.8, then 0. Residual load = load - wind - solar as a dashed teal #138374 line (the 'duck'): 0h 26.4, 4h 23.7, 6h 23.3, 8h 17.6, 10h 8.8, 12h 5.4, 14h 5.0, 16h 9.1, 18h 21.9, 20h 32.1, 22h 29.1. Label the belly 'duck's belly: residual load 5 GW at 14:00' and the neck 'evening ramp: +27 GW in 6 hours'. Bottom panel, day-ahead price EUR/MWh (-60 to 140), line #B4552F: 0h 88, 2h 78, 4h 76, 6h 73, 8h 45, 10h -1, 12h -31, 14h -43, 16h -3, 18h 76, 20h 126, 22h 107, 24h 88; shade the area below zero light blue and label 'negative prices: producers pay to deliver'. Phase 2 'A 1 GW / 2 GWh battery': show a battery icon charging between 12h and 14h (energy flows in, label 'buys 2 GWh at about -35 EUR/MWh: is paid 70,000 EUR') and discharging 19-21h (label 'sells 2 GWh at about 120 EUR/MWh: 240,000 EUR'), with a counter 'spread captured about 310,000 EUR minus losses (~15 %)'. Text >= 12 px, white background, no top/right axis lines.

spec.title: A May weekend day: the duck curve, negative prices and a battery
spec.caption: Average May 2025 weekend day in Germany (Energy-Charts). A cursor sweeps hour 0 to 24. Solar and wind push residual load (load - wind - solar, dashed teal) down to about 5 GW at 14:00, and day-ahead prices go negative. Then a 1 GW / 2 GWh battery charges at about -35 EUR/MWh and discharges into the evening ramp at about 120 EUR/MWh.
